info.title: Hifth app links
info.summary: Every address the Mac and iPad app answers to: plain links that turn the page, and x-callback-url requests that also answer the caller.
info.description:
The app is not a web server. These are `hifth://` links the operating system hands to the installed app: from a tapped link, from Shortcuts, from a script (`open`, `xcrun simctl openurl`). OpenAPI is used here as a way to write the contract down in one place that both people and tests read: `native/HifthTests/XCallbackTests.swift` runs every example under `x-examples` through the real parser, and `docs/design/app-url-scheme.html` is rendered from this file by `scripts/build-app-url-scheme.mjs`.

Two kinds of address. A **plain link** (`hifth:///hafs-kfqc/2:255`) turns the page and says nothing back; a bad one is ignored. An **x-callback-url request** (`hifth://x-callback-url/open?route=…&x-success=…`) does one action and then opens the caller's own address with the result, following the x-callback-url convention (x-callback-url.com): `x-success`, `x-error` and `x-cancel` name where to answer, and an error answer carries `errorCode` and `errorMessage`.

The route grammar is the web app's own hash, unchanged: `/<edition>/<target>[?query]`. The app only checks its shape; the web app decides what it means (`docs/query-params.md` lists the query keys).

servers.description: The installed Mac or iPad app. The scheme is registered by the app; nothing is sent over a network.

tags.name: Plain links
tags.description: Turn the page and say nothing back.

tags.name: x-callback-url
tags.description: Do one thing, then open the caller's x-success or x-error address with the result.

get.summary: Plain link: open the app at a verse, a page or a run of verses
get.description: The same string as the public site's `#/…` link, after `hifth://`. Three spellings are accepted because people paste all three: `hifth:///hafs-kfqc/2:255`, `hifth://hafs-kfqc/2:255`, and `hifth://open/#/hafs-kfqc/2:255` (a site link's tail). If the app is not running it launches there; if it is, it turns the page. Nothing is sent back, and a link that is not a route is ignored. Use `/x-callback-url/open` when you need to know it worked. The edition must be one the app ships; the others in the `Edition` list are refused the same way.

default.description: The page turns. No answer is sent to anyone.

get.summary: Open the app at a route, then tell the caller
get.description: Turns the page to the place named and, once the page is showing it, opens `x-success` with the `route` and the same place's public `url` added. Name the place plainly: `page=45`; `verse=2:255` (a run: `verse=2:47-48`) with `words=3-7` to pulse some of its words; or `surah=36` for a surah's context (its first verse, introduction first). `edition` defaults to `hafs-kfqc`. Say how to open it: `mode=note` (or `tool=note`) for the tool in hand, `open=commentary` for the verse's commentary or `open=context` for the commentary led by the surah's introduction, `view=one` or `view=two` for the layout. These three names are checked against the app's lists and a misspelt one is refused, so a caller learns about a typo instead of a page that quietly opened without it. Any other key the web app's links understand (`skin`, `field`, `via`, `trail`; see `docs/query-params.md`) is passed through as given, so `page=7&field=dark` opens page 7 on the night desk. `route` is the same thing as one string, for a caller that already holds a link; when both are given, `route` wins. If nothing names a place, or the place is not in the grammar, `x-error` is opened at once. If the page never shows it (a verse that does not exist, for instance), `x-error` is opened after about eight seconds with `route-not-shown`. With neither address given the page still turns, quietly.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: A page of the mus'haf, from 1. Give a page or a verse, not both.

parameters.name: verse
parameters.description: One verse as `surah:ayah`, or a run within one surah as `2:47-48` or `2:47-2:48`. The verse is selected on its page; a run is highlighted.

parameters.name: surah
parameters.description: A surah's context: opens its first verse with the commentary sheet led by the surah's introduction, as `verse=N:1&open=context` would. 1 to 114. Give one of page, verse or surah.

parameters.name: words
parameters.description: Which words of the verse to pulse: `3-7`, or `5` for one word. Needs `verse`.

parameters.name: edition
parameters.description: Which mus'haf, by its id. Defaults to `hafs-kfqc`, the only one shipped today. A name not in the `Edition` list, or one not shipped yet, is refused with `bad-route` and a message naming the shipped ids.

parameters.name: route
parameters.description: The place as one string in the web app's link grammar, `/<edition>/<target>[?query]`, for a caller that already holds a link. Percent-encode it, or a `&` inside its query is read as the end of this parameter. Wins over `page`/`verse` when both are given.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: The mode the app opens in: the page tool put in hand on arrival, named by the word on its button. The same thing as `tool`; give one or the other. A name not in the list is refused with `bad-route`.

parameters.name: tool
parameters.description: The web app's own name for `mode`. Passed through as `tool=` in the route.

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: A panel open on arrival. `commentary` opens the named verse's commentary (tafsir); `context` opens it led by the surah's introduction. Both need a verse, and exist only in a build that holds commentary (the private pitch build) — the public app opens the verse and drops the panel. The rest are the app's own panels: go-to, about, the revision record, the record at juz scope, the tajweed colour key, the mus'haf picker, the tips strip, a verse's look-alikes, a verse's roots. A name not in the list is refused with `bad-route`.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: One page or two side by side on arrival, on a screen wide enough for two. A phone always shows one.

parameters.name: skin
parameters.description: `tajweed` turns the tajweed colours on. One of the web app's own keys, passed through; the others in `docs/query-params.md` pass the same way.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The desk colour the mus'haf lies on, e.g. `dark` or `tan`. Passed through; an unknown value falls back to the default desk.

default.description: Nothing comes back on this address. The answer is one of the callbacks below.

get.summary: Ask what the app is showing
get.description: Opens `x-success` with the `route` on screen and its public `url`. If nothing is on screen yet (the app was just launched by this request), the answer waits for the first page to show. There is no error case beyond a missing `x-success`, which means no answer.

default.description: Nothing comes back on this address. The answer is the success callback below.

edition.name: edition
edition.description: Which mus'haf, by its id. Only a shipped one opens; the list is `Edition` below.

target.name: target
target.description: A page (`p45`), a verse (`2:255`), a run of verses (`2:47-2:48` or `2:47-48`). Every number starts from 1.

routeQuery.name: query
routeQuery.description: Any of the web app's own keys, e.g. `w=3-7` (some words of the verse), `skin=tajweed`, `field=dark`. The full list and what a bad value does is `docs/query-params.md`.

xSuccess.name: x-success
xSuccess.description: Where to answer when the action worked. Any app's address (`shortcuts://…`, `drafts://…`, `https://…`). The answer's parameters are added to its query. Ignored if it points back into this app, or at a file or a script.

xError.name: x-error
xError.description: Where to answer when the action failed. Opened with `errorCode` and `errorMessage` added, as the x-callback-url convention names them. Same safety rule as x-success.

xCancel.name: x-cancel
xCancel.description: Accepted for completeness and never opened: neither action here can be cancelled by the reader.

xSource.name: x-source
xSource.description: The calling app's name, per the convention. Accepted and not used; the app shows no 'back to' button.

Edition.description: Which mus'haf, by its id. The app's own list, copied here with an English name and whether the mus'haf is actually in the build. A name not in the list, or one not shipped yet, is refused: a plain link is ignored, a request is answered with `bad-route` and a message that names the shipped ids. The shipped one is the default when a request names none.

x-editions.name: Warsh · Libyan Endowments print
x-editions.reason: licensed for non-commercial use only; needs permission before it can be added

x-editions.name: Qalun · Libyan Endowments print
x-editions.reason: licensed for non-commercial use only; needs permission before it can be added

Route.description: `/<edition>/<target>[?query]` — the web app's own link, without the `#`. The edition must be one the app ships (see `Edition`).

ErrorCode.description: `missing-route`: open named no page, verse, surah or route. `bad-route`: the place is not in the grammar (a page of 0, two places at once, words without a verse, a surah past 114), or a mode, panel or view name not in the app's lists, or an edition not in the list or not shipped yet. `unknown-action`: the path after x-callback-url is not open or current. `route-not-shown`: the place was accepted but the page never showed it.

get.summary: Opened by the app when the action worked
get.description: The caller's own address, with two parameters added to whatever query it already had. Values are percent-encoded so a route's own `?w=3-7` cannot be mistaken for a parameter of the answer.

parameters.name: route
parameters.description: What is on screen, in the same shape the caller sends (no `#`).

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The same place on the public site, ready to share.

default.description: Whatever the caller does with it.

get.summary: Opened by the app when the action failed

parameters.name: errorMessage
parameters.description: One plain sentence for a person, e.g. `not a route: chapter-2`.

default.description: Whatever the caller does with it.

x-examples.note: A plain link with three slashes: the route is the path.
Two slashes: the edition lands where a host would be. Still a route.
A site link's tail pasted after hifth://open/, fragment and all.
Page numbers start at 1. A plain link that is not a route is ignored, silently.
A mus'haf we know but do not ship yet. A plain link is ignored, like any link that is not a route; a request says why.
Open page 45, said plainly. No encoding needed.
Select Al-Baqarah 2:255 and pulse its words 3 to 7.
Highlight a run of verses in tajweed colours on the night desk. skin and field pass through to the web app.
Straight into a verse's commentary (tafsir), in a build that holds it.
The same note, led by al-Baqarah's introduction.
A surah's context: its first verse, introduction first.
Open in note mode: the note tool is in hand on arrival.
A mode that is not in the list is refused, not quietly dropped.
The panel is called commentary, not tafsir.
A mus'haf we know but do not ship yet: refused as not shipped, with the shipped ids named.
A name not in the edition list, inside a whole route: refused with the list.
A page and a verse at once: the app cannot know which you meant.
Words without a verse.
Open a verse from Shortcuts; the answer runs one shortcut on success and another on failure.
A route with its own query, percent-encoded so its & is not read as the end of the route.
No route given: x-error is opened at once with errorCode=missing-route.
Not in the grammar: errorCode=bad-route, errorMessage=not a route: chapter-2.
Ask what is on screen; Drafts gets a new draft with route=… and url=… in its query.
Only open and current exist. Anything else answers errorCode=unknown-action.
An answer address that points back into this app is dropped, so a request cannot answer itself for ever.
